1. Continuation after a timeout kill: one turn on the same thread/session (codex resume, agy

   900)); a usable reply is ingested like a first-turn reply (`bridge_outcome` "usable reply
   (after a timeout continuation)", ledger `timeout_continue {thread, wall_seconds, outcome,

   failure; panel members continue in their own process (the guard grows by `-ContinueSec`).
2. Partial salvage: `<NN>-<engine>-<slug>.partial.md` from the captured stream (agent messages,
   reasoning, tool calls, the resume command as a footer), ledger `partial_reply`, the summary
   names it; `-Thread` accepts a killed agy conversation / muse session for a manual resume.

   `-Range <git range>` for diff-review/acceptance: `git diff --shortstat` numbers in the prompt

   every surface; LAST FAILURE shows any limit that still blocks; the listing prints where its
   health comes from (`endpoint health:` naming the ledger directory) - the T2 disagreement was

2: .SYNOPSIS
3:     SessionStart hook: one line saying which reviewers are out right now, and until when.
4: 
5: .DESCRIPTION
6:     Runs at the start of a Claude Code session in any project where the plugin is
7:     enabled (hooks/hooks.json). Prints ONE line to stdout, which Claude Code adds to the
8:     agent's context (wave 24, D14-D17 - the line `codex-providers.ps1 -Short` prints):
9: 
10:         codex-consult: out - openai :: gpt-6-astra (until Sun 20:35, in 2d 10h), gemini :: *
11:         (until Sun 21:30, in 2d 11h); 9 of 11 reviewers available
12: 
13:     or `codex-consult: all 11 reviewers available`. Every roster entry is judged with the
14:     roster walk's own verdict (Select-PanelMembers -All: credentials, the launch invariant,
15:     the endpoint health of THIS repository's ledgers - an auth failure, a usage limit with a
16:     reset ahead, one without a reset for 60 minutes after it was hit); the entries of one
17:     endpoint group that share the state collapse to `<label> :: *`; reset times are LOCAL
18:     with a rounded relative hint; nothing is cut. An entry whose check needs the network (the
19:     agy engine's `agy models`) is `not checked` here - "..., 2 not checked" in the count -
20:     unless THIS repository's ledgers hold a usable reply on that endpoint from the last 60
21:     minutes (then it is available); a recorded auth failure or usage limit still shows it
22:     out. The muse engine's sign-in check reads ~/.config/muse/auth.json locally and runs here
23:     too, as does its billing guard (`meta :: <model> (refused: META_API_KEY is set)`).
24:     Without a roster: the providers of the Codex config ("... (no reviewer roster)").
25: 
26:     When the Codex CLI is not on PATH: `codex-consult: codex CLI not found on PATH - follow
27:     the setup-providers skill`. Everything else (an unreadable config, an unusable roster, a
28:     crash inside the check) is reported in the same one-line form and never fails the
29:     session: the exit code is always 0. No network call, no lock, nothing written: it runs
30:     `codex-providers.ps1 -Short -Json -NoNetwork` and prints the `line` of its object.
31: 
32:     Cost: about one second (`codex login status` for the built-in openai), once per
33:     session. Disable the hook by disabling the plugin's hooks in Claude Code settings.
34: 
35:     Runs on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.
36: #>
37: [CmdletBinding()]
38: param(
39:     # Where consultations are stored (endpoint health is read from every task ledger
40:     # under it). Relative paths resolve against the git repo root of the current directory.
41:     [string]$CollabDir = '.collab'
42: )
43: 
44: $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
45: $line = ''
46: try {
47:     $providers = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'codex-providers.ps1'
48:     $psExe = (Get-Process -Id $PID).Path
49:     $codex = Get-Command codex -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
50:     if (-not $codex) {
51:         $line = 'codex-consult: codex CLI not found on PATH - follow the setup-providers skill before consulting a reviewer'
52:     } else {
53:         $previous = $ErrorActionPreference
54:         $ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
55:         $raw = @(& $psExe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $providers -Short -Json -NoNetwork -CollabDir $CollabDir 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "$_" })
56:         $code = $LASTEXITCODE
57:         $ErrorActionPreference = $previous
58:         $jsonStart = -1
59:         for ($i = 0; $i -lt $raw.Count; $i++) { if ($raw[$i] -match '^\s*\{') { $jsonStart = $i; break } }
60:         $obj = $null
61:         if ($jsonStart -ge 0) {
62:             try { $obj = (($raw[$jsonStart..($raw.Count - 1)]) -join "`n") | ConvertFrom-Json } catch { $obj = $null }
63:         }
64:         $text = $(if ($obj) { [string]$obj.line } else { '' })
65:         if ($text -match '^codex-consult: ' -and $text -notmatch "[`r`n]") {
66:             $line = $text
67:         } else {
68:             $first = (@($raw | Where-Object { $_ -and $_.Trim() }) | Select-Object -First 1)
69:             if (-not $first) { $first = "codex-providers.ps1 exited $code without output" }
70:             $line = "codex-consult: reviewer check failed - $first"
71:         }
72:     }
73: } catch {
74:     $msg = ("$($_.Exception.Message)" -replace '\s+', ' ').Trim()
75:     if ($msg.Length -gt 120) { $msg = $msg.Substring(0, 117) + '...' }
76:     $line = "codex-consult: reviewer check failed - $msg"
77: }
78: Write-Output $line
79: exit 0

## 2. New defects in wave 24 (what I verified vs inferred)
Verified in code: the continuation gates (`-ContinueSec` 0, unknown thread, survivors, tree change, quota/auth in the killed turn's own stream — codex-consult.ps1:2999-3022), muse's `-Fresh` guard before every turn incl. the continuation (666, 2621; muse adapter 3757-3769), the codex `resume <thread>` argv mirroring the main turn (3031-3038 vs 2372-2392), thread verification of the continuation (3070, 3088), salvage conditions and the partial file/footer/resume command (3402-3456), `-Thread` accepting a killed agy/muse candidate via `partial_reply` (Find-ThreadEntry), the second tree check after all extra turns (3345-3352), purpose timeouts and `-Range` (788-802, 900-918, 1046-1064, 2290-2292), the panel member inheritance and guard growth (837-843, 1238-1267, common.ps1:5326-5332), and the availability surfaces above. harness-visibility has exactly 76 checks incl. ## 3. Verdict
**ACCEPT.** No blocker or major remains; all wave-24 prior findings are fixed and the new code is internally consistent with the documented D14–D17 behavior. Blockers: none.
